title: Execute Conformance Assessment Against the Manifest

filesChanged.change: Added the AssessConformance engine: `assessConformance`, `assessmentViolations`, `renderAssessment`, `CONFORMANCE_ITEM_ID`, `parseAnnotationSink`, the `demoted` claim state and its required `ClaimAssessment` record. `main()` now reads the annotation sink, feeds acceptance-1 violations into task 10's `renderReport(manifest, violations)` seam, and prints the per-level per-role verdict.

Extended with 24 tests covering the assessment engine and the three acceptance criteria. One existing test was REFINED (not weakened) and two new tests pin the guard it used to carry — see `refinedExistingTest`.

Added 5 black-box assessment cases driving a real MCP host over HTTP and observing the host's own request log, audit trail and wire responses. The pre-existing EAP-FUNC-001 binding and all 41 original assertions are untouched.

Added 1 case that pins the fact behind two client-role demotions: the adapter answers a refusal with advice and never issues the next request. Carries NO conformance items — it is the guard on the demotions, not evidence for them.
14 items DEMOTED (claimed -> demoted) with a `claim.assessment` record each. No item promoted. No clause reworded. Source digest and line pins untouched.

attributionChannelDecision.chosen: the existing `items[]` field of the Discharge Annotation (packages/mcp-server/test/verification/annotate.ts:83)
attributionChannelDecision.rejected: reusing `asserts`/`coversPartially`, which are keyed to Scenario Register ids
attributionChannelDecision.justification: `items[]` is already a separate field, is already excluded from `buildLinks` in reconcile-traceability.ts (only `record.scenarios` produces links), and is validated by nobody against the Scenario Register. Conformance Item Ids therefore cannot leak into the Traceability Map as scenario coverage. Belt and braces: `CONFORMANCE_ITEM_ID` is /^EAP-L[0-3]-\d{3}$/ and the Scenario `IDENTIFIER` is /^EAP-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$/; `L0`..`L3` contain a digit, so NEITHER regex can match the other's identifiers. An id in the wrong channel is reported as a violation rather than silently counted, and both directions are pinned by test.
attributionChannelDecision.sideEffectAccepted: `recordIdentity` in reconcile-traceability.ts includes `record.items`, so adding items to an existing annotated case changes that record's identity. The stale sink was deleted and the suite re-run, as that script instructs.

verdict.policy: Client and host verdicts are independent and are never merged into one pass rate (ADR-0007: L0-L1 certify clients, L2-L4 certify hosts). Declared exclusions are neither failures nor green.

predicatesThatCouldNotBeObserved.systemicCause: The host's audit log records ADMISSIONS ONLY. The complete set of EAP rows ever appended is PromotionProposed, KnowledgeContested and RecallProgressed. `cognitive.initiate` and `cognitive.propose` write nothing. Ten of the fourteen demotions reduce to this one fact.
secondaryCauses: No egress log exists on the host (EAP-L2-007).
No client in the repository issues a request in response to a refusal (EAP-L0-003, EAP-L1-005).
No horizon read surface is published, so horizon state is unreadable by an assessor (EAP-L3-001).
The EAP tool surface carries no anchor and no derivation field, so those submissions cannot be made over transport (EAP-L2-003, EAP-L2-009).
No claim-dependency corpus is constructible over the EAP wire (EAP-L3-008).
predicatesThatCouldNotBeObserved.hostRequestLogGap: index.ts:275 harvests `reasons` from a refused tool result, but an EAP refusal carries `refusal.code`. Every EAP refusal is therefore logged as `verdict:"refused", reasons:[]` — the fact of refusal without its taxonomy code.

refinedExistingTest.was: test("claims L0, L1 and L2 in full") — asserted every L0/L1/L2 item is `claimed`
refinedExistingTest.now: test("keeps L0, L1 and L2 out of `not-yet-claimed`: a claim leaves only through a demotion")
refinedExistingTest.whyThisIsNotAWeakening: Task 10's rule encoded a judgement made by READING SOURCE, which was the only evidence then available; task 11 refuted 14 of those claims against real transport and has demotion authority. The guard task 10 built is intact and separately pinned — an L0/L1/L2 item downgraded to `not-yet-claimed` is STILL a violation (validateManifest, and the untouched test "catches an L2 item downgraded out of its full claim"). The refined rule additionally REQUIRES every demotion to carry an assessment record, and two NEW tests pin that a demotion without one, and an assessment record on a still-claimed item, both fail the gate. Strictly more is enforced after this change than before it.

foundButNotOwned.finding: The host's audit log records admissions and never refusals. Ten of fourteen demotions reduce to this. A refusal is visible on the wire and as `verdict:"refused"` in the request log, but is absent from the audit trail an EAP assessor is told to read.
foundButNotOwned.owner: human architect — EAP behaviour, not test tooling

foundButNotOwned.finding: index.ts:275 `toolVerdict` harvests `reasons` from a refused result, but EAP refusals carry `refusal.code`. Every EAP refusal is logged as `reasons:[]` — the fact of refusal without its code. A one-line fix would materially strengthen the host request log as a conformance surface.

Two manifest items name an `evidence.surface` that cannot carry the limb they describe: EAP-L0-002's cursor limb (the request log strips the query string by design, log.ts:118) and EAP-L2-002's audit limb (vacuous — no refusal rows). Both discharge on genuine host records; the labels are wrong. Out of scope here: the manifest may only be modified to demote.
EAP-L1-002 referent ambiguity: `ciclo de changeset` may mean the graph changeset subsystem (audited, complete) or the EAP epistemic ladder (unaudited). Demoted rather than decided.

Caller-blindness within a single tenant is unproven and may be unprovable by construction: two identities cannot submit identical content twice in one tenant, because the first submission moves the state the second is judged against.
foundButNotOwned.owner: human architect — may need a clause reading, not a test

honestSummary: Apêndice D was claimed at 22 of 27 items from a reading of source. Assessed against real transport, 8 discharge. The gap is not mostly missing tests — it is missing host records: this host's audit log does not record refusals, and most of Apêndice D's evidence predicates are written over refusal rows. One of task 10's three referrals was refuted (EAP-L2-008 now discharges), two were confirmed, and the weakest claimed row (EAP-L2-001) now has a real four-identity test. No item was promoted. No clause was reworded. No existing test was weakened.
